business_scope.primary_industry_name: Commercial CGI Visual Effects and 3D Character Animation

meta_jurisdiction_context.jurisdiction_name_en: Swiss Confederation (Swiss federal jurisdiction with cantonal registration and supervision)
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Switzerland–EU Free Trade Agreement of 1972 and Bilateral Agreements I & II between Switzerland and the EU
EFTA Free Trade Network in force with more than 40 states and territories
Double Taxation Agreements concluded with more than 100 jurisdictions, including Germany, France, United Kingdom, United States (1996/2009) and China (2013 protocol)
Bilateral Investment Protection Agreements concluded by Switzerland, including the Switzerland–China Investment Agreement (1986)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Federal Act on Combating Money Laundering and Terrorist Financing (AMLA/GwG), SR 955.0, as amended and in force from 1 January 2023; Ordinance on the Transparency of Legal Entities (Transparenzverordnung), SR 955.062, establishing the Swiss beneficial owner register for Aktiengesellschaften effective 1 November 2023; Swiss Code of Obligations (CO/OR), SR 220, Art. 640, Art. 643, Art. 950 and Art. 954; Swiss Criminal Code, SR 311.0, Art. 305bis and Art. 305ter; FINMA Anti-Money Laundering Ordinance (AMLO-FINMA), SR 955.03.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized deed of incorporation (public instrument) including the Articles of Association, executed pursuant to Art. 640 of the Swiss Code of Obligations
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary Public licensed in the Canton of the statutory seat (e.g., Zug, Zurich or Geneva)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille issued by the competent Cantonal authority; alternatively consular legalization by the Swiss Embassy or Consulate of the destination state if the destination is not a party to the 1961 Hague Apostille Convention

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of entry in the Cantonal Commercial Register / Handelsregisterauszug confirming registration of the AG
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille issued by the competent Cantonal authority; consular legalization for non-Hague destination states

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: UBO disclosure declaration and extract of the beneficial owner register entry submitted under the Transparenzverordnung (SR 955.062)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Federal Department of Justice and Police (FDJP) / Transparency Register Office
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Electronic extracts are issued by the Federal Transparency Register; a certified notarized paper printout can be apostilled by the Cantonal authority when required by foreign counterparties

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Registered-office and domiciliation agreement evidencing the physical address for legal service, pursuant to Art. 643 CO
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille where the document is notarized; otherwise attestation by the service provider and acceptance by the Cantonal Commercial Register Office

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized limited power of attorney authorizing counsel to execute the incorporation filing
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary Public in the Canton of the statutory seat
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille; consular legalization for non-Hague destination states

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory downstream PEP and sanctions screening under Art. 6–9a AMLA, AMLO-FINMA, and the FATF 40 Recommendations. Screening must cover (i) the Swiss State Secretariat for Economic Affairs (SECO) financial sanctions lists and Federal Council embargo ordinances issued under the Embargo Act (SR 946.2), (ii) the United Nations Security Council consolidated sanctions list, (iii) the European Union consolidated financial sanctions list, and (iv) OFAC SDN and primary sanctions lists for USD-denominated rails upon activation of Wise_B2B or SWIFT wire services. Politically exposed persons (PEPs) require enhanced due diligence, including verification of source of funds, prior approval by senior management, and continuous monitoring. Suspicious activity must be reported to the Money Laundering Reporting Office Switzerland (MROS) within two business days under Art. 9 AMLA.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: ZEFIX (Zentraler Firmenindex / Central Business Index), operated by the Federal Office of Justice, is the official search platform for the Swiss commercial register; the actual name-clearance and registration procedure is conducted through the Cantonal Commercial Register Office (Handelsregisteramt) using the electronic commercial register filing system (easiHR/TEREOS).
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The firm name must not be misleading under Art. 950 and Art. 954 CO, must be written in Latin script in at least one official Swiss language (German, French or Italian) of the canton of the statutory seat, and may contain English or other Latin-alphabet terms provided they are distinctive and do not cause confusion as to legal form. The legal form suffix 'Aktiengesellschaft' or the abbreviation 'AG' must be in an official Swiss language; transliteration of foreign company names into Latin script is permitted when the original script is not Latin, subject to phonetic accuracy and distinctiveness. Cyrillic, Arabic, Chinese or other non-Latin scripts are not registerable as the statutory firm name.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Bank; Banque; Banca; Sparkasse or similar terms suggesting banking activity, requiring a Swiss banking license
Insurance; Versicherung; Assurances; Reassurance, requiring FINMA insurance licensing
Swiss; Suisse; Svizzera; Switzerland; Helvetia, and equivalent Swissness indicators, requiring consent under the Swissness legislation and use of the Swiss coat of arms statute
Federal; Eidgenössisch; Confederation; Eidgenossenschaft, implying state affiliation and requiring authorization
Swiss federal coat of arms, Swiss cross, and protective Red Cross emblems, which are statutorily protected
Börse; SIX; Stock Exchange; Exchange, implying stock-exchange operation and requiring regulatory authorization
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Switzerland does not provide a statutory name-reservation register; however, a preliminary name-clearance decision (Vorentscheid) is issued by the Cantonal Commercial Register Office and is honored for approximately 30 calendar days. Upon formal rejection, the applicant shall, within 30 days of the rejection notice, either (i) submit an amended name for a new Vorentscheid without further notarial act, or (ii) file a written administrative appeal with the Cantonal Administrative Court (Verwaltungsgericht) in accordance with the applicable Cantonal Administrative Procedure Act. The appeal must state the legal grounds, annex the registrar's rejection letter, the Vorentscheid and the Articles of Association name clause. A final appeal to the Swiss Federal Supreme Court may be brought under Art. 82 et seq. of the Federal Supreme Court Act (BGG) only where a legal question of national significance arises. It is recommended to obtain a written trademark-clearance opinion from a Swiss IP attorney before re-filing.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: For a low-risk Standard industrial classification (ISIC 5911 / NAICS 512110 – Commercial CGI Visual Effects and 3D Character Animation), a registered-office and domiciliation arrangement with a Swiss corporate service provider is accepted if the provider maintains a physical office at the registered address, receives postal and legal service, provides a dedicated letterbox and board-meeting facilities on demand, and files the required commercial register declarations. A pure PO box, a mail-forwarding address or a digital-only virtual office without physical staff and reception capability is not permissible under Art. 643 CO and the Commercial Register Ordinance.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low. The estimated annual probability of an unannounced physical on-site inspection by the Cantonal Commercial Register Office or cantonal tax authorities for a low-risk animation and VFX production company is approximately 2–5% during the first post-incorporation year. Unannounced on-site visits occur mainly where there are substantial grounds for suspected sham-residence, tax evasion, money-laundering or insolvency abuse; standard tax audits in Switzerland are announced in writing in advance.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Notarial execution of the deed of incorporation including approval of Articles of Association under Art. 640 CO
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Cantonal Notary Public at the statutory seat
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory Cantonal Notarial Tariff; prevailing market range for a simple single-shareholder AG deed is USD 350–550

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Commercial register entry fee for registration of a newly formed Aktiengesellschaft with share capital of CHF 100,000
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Official Cantonal and Federal fee schedules; typical amount CHF 545–650

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Application fee for preliminary firm-name clearance (Vorentscheid) before the Cantonal Commercial Register Office
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Cantonal fee schedule for administrative clearances; typical amount USD 100–300

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: First-time notification and registration of the beneficial owner in the federal Transparency Register under SR 955.062
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Federal Department of Justice and Police (FDJP) / Transparency Register Office
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: No statutory notification fee is charged; costs are absorbed in the notary and counsel mandate

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Swiss federal stamp duty on the issuance of shares at incorporation
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory Stamp Duty Act exemption: issuance of share capital below CHF 1,000,000 is not subject to federal stamp tax

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Hague Apostille legalization of the deed of incorporation, commercial register excerpt and UBO declaration for cross-border use
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Per-document statutory fee under the 1961 Hague Apostille Convention; typical amount CHF 20–50 per document

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Swiss corporate counsel fees for pre-incorporation due diligence, constitution drafting, regulatory review and filing management
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark for a turnkey low-risk AG formation: USD 1,000–2,000 flat fee

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Annual registered-office and domiciliation service including physical reception, mail handling, compliance support and UBO registry coordination
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark for a low-risk AG in Zug, Zurich or Geneva: USD 240–900 per year

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Swiss Code of Obligations (Obligationenrecht / Code des obligations), Arts. 620-763 (Aktiengesellschaft); incorporation formalities per Arts. 626-637 OR; registration and legal personality per Art. 643 OR and Arts. 62-95 of the Commercial Register Ordinance (Handelsregisterverordnung, HRegV); name-control rules per Arts. 950-951 OR.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Cantonal Commercial Register Office (Handelsregisteramt / Registre du commerce) of the canton of the registered office, operating under the supervisory authority of the Federal Commercial Register Authority at the Federal Department of Justice and Police (Bundesamt für Justiz, BJ).
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Notarized Deed of Incorporation (Errichtungsakt) including the Articles of Association (Statuten), accompanied by the Board's Declaration of Acceptance (Annahmeerklärung) and the bank's blocked-account capital confirmation, filed through the e-register/eBAS electronic filing portal of the competent cantonal registry.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: Minimum share capital CHF 100,000; at least 20% of the nominal value of each share, and in aggregate no less than CHF 50,000, must be paid up in cash before registration. The paid-up amount must be confirmed by a Swiss-regulated bank via a blocked capital deposit account (Sperrkonto), with funds held at the company's disposal and subject to the Swiss Anti-Money-Laundering Act verification of all ultimate beneficial owners.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: The Board of Directors of [Company Name] AG, constituted by the public Deed of Incorporation, resolves as follows: (1) The subscription of the entire share capital of CHF 100,000, divided into 1,000 registered shares of CHF 100 nominal value each, is confirmed and ratified; the blocked-account confirmation of the paid-up capital of CHF 50,000 from a Swiss-regulated bank is accepted. (2) The registered office of the Company is adopted and established at [Street Address], [City], Canton of [Canton]. (3) [Name] is appointed Chairperson of the Board; [Name] is appointed Company Secretary; [Name] is appointed Managing Director with individual signatory authority (signature à titre individuel). This resolution takes effect immediately.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Company name clearance and availability verification
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Federal Central Business Index (Zefix) and the competent Cantonal Commercial Register Office (Handelsregisteramt) via zefix.ch
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Screen the proposed single or combined name on the Zefix public index to confirm that the name is distinctive, truthful, and not misleading under Arts. 950-951 OR. Where the canton offers the facility, file a name reservation application with the Cantonal Commercial Register Office. Verify that the corporate suffix 'AG' replaces 'SA' and that the business-purpose wording covers animation and visual effects production.
required_dossiers: Proposed long-form and short-form company names
Drafted business-purpose clause (ISIC 5911 animation/VFX production)
Identity details of each founding shareholder
Cantonal name-reservation application form (where applicable)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registry rejects the name for lack of distinctiveness or misleading effect, file an amended application with a revised distinctive element; in most cantons a corrected re-filing within 30 days is processed without a new fee.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execution of the incorporation deed before a Swiss notary
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Cantonal Public Notary (Öffentlicher Notar / Notaire) of the canton of the registered office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: All founders must appear personally before the notary. The notary authenticates the Deed of Incorporation, verifies the adequacy of the Articles of Association against Arts. 626-627 OR, records the subscription of shares, certifies the apportionment of formation costs, and procures the founders' signed declaration concerning paid-up share capital. The notary subsequently submits the electronic signature data to the Commercial Register system.
required_dossiers: Valid passport or state identity document of each natural-person founder
Final draft of the Articles of Association (Statuten)
Bank blocked-account confirmation (Sperrkonto-Bestätigung) showing CHF 50,000 available
Completed AML/KYC beneficial-owner attestation form
If a corporate founder exists, its duly authorized board resolution
Power of attorney for any representative founder
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Formal deficiencies (typographical or evidentiary omissions) are cured by a supplementary notarial instrument on the same day; substantive changes to the articles require a new notarial sitting and an updated deed, with additional notarial fees.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Opening of the blocked capital deposit account and payment of share capital
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Swiss-regulated bank or licensed securities firm authorized by FINMA to issue capital confirmations
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a blocked share-capital deposit account (Sperrkonto / compte de réserves) in the name of the company to be formed. Transfer from each founder the amount credited towards the subscribed shares so that the aggregate paid-up balance reaches at least CHF 50,000. The bank performs AMLA verification of each beneficial owner and issues a blocked-account confirmation stating that the funds are at the future company's disposal and blocked until successful Commercial Register registration.
required_dossiers: Company formation data sheet and draft articles for bank opening
Founders' list with subscription amounts and bank details
Identity and beneficial-owner declarations for AML checks
Bank's standard blocked-account instruction template (Sperrkonto-Bestätigung)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank declines to issue the attestation due to outstanding AML docs, provide the additional KYC evidence within 5 business days or re-source the account to another FINMA-licensed bank; if the transferred amount is below CHF 50,000, the founders effect a top-up remittance before re-requesting confirmation.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Electronic filing with the Cantonal Commercial Register
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Cantonal Commercial Register Office (Handelsregisteramt) of the registered-office canton via the e-register / eBAS system
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Counsel or the notary submits the notarized Deed of Incorporation, the Articles of Association, the board acceptance declarations, the blocked-account capital confirmation, and the signature-authorization specimen for each signatory. The registry checks formal correctness under OR and HRegV, verifies the registered office address with the municipality, and issues the registration order upon satisfaction of all requirements.
required_dossiers: Notarized Deed of Incorporation in public form
Articles of Association (Statuten)
Founders' and Board declarations under Art. 102-103 HRegV
Bank blocked-account capital confirmation
List of shareholders and notarized subscription signatures
Signed specimen signatures for each authorized officer
Municipal consent concerning the usableness of the registered office (if required by the canton)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: The registry issues a deficiency notice for cure within 30 days; counsel or the notary files a supplementary declaration or amended schedule on the same portal. A contested refusal may be appealed to the Cantonal Administrative Court within the statutory appeal period and ultimately to the Swiss Federal Supreme Court on matters of law.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Registration entry, SHAB publication, and issuance of the registry extract
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Swiss Official Gazette of Commerce (Schweizerisches Handelsblatt, SHAB) — publication is triggered automatically by the registry; UID registration is confirmed by the Swiss Federal Statistical Office system
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upon entry in the Commercial Register, the company acquires legal personality as of that moment (Art. 643 OR). The registry transmits the registration notice to the SHAB for mandatory publication. The company then obtains its official Commercial Register extract and its Swiss Company Identification Number (UID CHE-xxx) for use with tax authorities and banks.
required_dossiers: Registration order and system-generated confirmation from the Cantonal Commercial Register
Official registry extract request (receipt of registration order serves as proof)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a third party files an objection against the publication, the registry sets a short correction period; counsel must file a defensive submission demonstrating the groundlessness of the objection, with intervention before the Commercial Register Appeals Commission if the objection is not lifted.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Federal, cantonal tax and social security registrations
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Federal Tax Administration (ESTV/AFC) — Main VAT Office, Cantonal Tax Administration (Kantonale Steuerverwaltung), and the Cantonal Compensation Office (AHV-Ausgleichskasse / OASI)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Send the corporate registration questionnaire to the cantonal tax administration for income-tax, net-wealth-tax and withholding-tax registration; register as an employer with the compensation office for AHV/IV/EO contributions (mandatory from the first employee); assess VAT liability — mandatory registration is required once worldwide turnover exceeds CHF 100,000, with voluntary registration available for production companies issuing invoices with input-VAT deductions.
required_dossiers: Certified copy of the Commercial Register extract showing UID
Lease agreement or proof of registered-office premises
Completed cantonal tax registration form for legal entities
Employer registration questionnaire for AHV/IV/EO
VAT registration form (Form 14) if turnover threshold is met or voluntary registration is elected
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the cantonal tax authority fails to confirm registration within 20 working days, counsel submits a written reminder; in the event VAT registration has been omitted while the turnover threshold is exceeded, a retroactive registration with back-dated VAT assessments is permissible, and any late-filing penalty can be mitigated by voluntary self-disclosure.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Municipal business supervision and workplace operational clearances
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Municipal Administration of the registered-office municipality (Gemeindeverwaltung), Cantonal Fire Police (Feuerpolizei), and SUVA or an approved private accident insurer under the Accident Insurance Act (UVG)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Notify the municipality of the commercial use of the registered office as an animation studio, obtain the municipal business-registration confirmation (where the canton requires a Gewerbebewilligung), and complete the fire-safety clearance of the office premises by the fire police. Register all personnel with SUVA or a licensed private accident insurer for non-occupational and occupational accident cover, and adopt the statutory workplace health and safety measures for computer-screen-based workplaces.
required_dossiers: Lease agreement or title deed for the studio/office premises
Fire-safety concept and evacuation plan approved by the Feuerpolizei
Employee register and payroll data for accident-insurance registration
Workplace regulations (Arbeitsreglement) where more than one employee is engaged
Technical data sheets for workstation lighting, screens and office layouts
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Where the fire-police clearance identifies structural deficiencies, coordinate with the landlord to obtain a building-permit addendum and then schedule a follow-up inspection; if the municipality refuses confirmation on zoning grounds, apply for an exceptional provisional use authorization or relocate the registered office to an approved commercial zone, with re-registration at the Commercial Register.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: No sectoral industrial licensing board is applicable to commercial CGI and 3D animation production under ISIC 5911; general municipal business supervision (Gewerbepolizei) and the Cantonal Department of Economic Affairs (Amt für Wirtschaft und Arbeit) provide only routine registration and labor-market oversight.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: No statutory operating or manufacturing permit is required for an animation/VFX studio under the Swiss Federal Act on Radio and Television (RTVA), which governs broadcasting rather than content production; the company operates under its Commercial Register entry, the municipal business-registration confirmation, and any applicable work/residence approvals for non-EEA creative personnel.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Federal Office for the Environment (FOEN / Bundesamt für Umwelt, BAFU) and the competent cantonal environmental protection office (Amt für Umwelt) of the registered-office canton
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt from environmental impact assessment: digital 3D animation and VFX studio activities do not appear in Annex 1 of the Environmental Impact Assessment Ordinance (UVPV), hence no preliminary assessment or full EIA report is triggered
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No industrial wastewater, VOC or particulate-emission thresholds apply to an office-based production studio; applicable compliance obligations are limited to the Swiss Ordinance on Waste Movements and the VVEA for e-waste, disposal of IT hardware, batteries and lamps through the licensed SENS/ENSI recycling systems, and the general precautionary principle under the Environmental Protection Act (USG) for procurement and office energy use

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Mandatory fire-safety certification from the municipal Feuerpolizei confirming compliance with the cantonal fire-protection ordinance; structural-load and occupancy clearance evidenced by the landlord's valid commercial building permit and lease; registration with SUVA or a licensed private accident insurer under the UVG for occupational coverage; occupational-health clearance for screen workplaces under the Labour Act (ArG) including the 4-hour maximum continuous screen work regime, workplace ergonomics, lighting and ventilation standards.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Swiss Federal Tax Administration (Eidgenössische Steuerverwaltung / ESTV — Administration fédérale des contributions / AFC), official portal: www.estv.admin.ch (ePortal for VAT returns and registrations)
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign company without a Swiss registered office that performs taxable supplies in Switzerland must apply online to the Swiss Federal Tax Administration for a Swiss VAT number (UID/MWST-Nr. / UID/TVA). The application is submitted through the FTA's ePortal (Login mit SwissID/CH-LOGIN) using the 'Formular 100 Änderungsmeldung / Registrierung' or the official ePortal registration module. The company must state its foreign registration, actual activity in Switzerland, estimated Swiss turnover, and appoint a Swiss tax representative if it has no Swiss establishment. The UID is generally granted within days; there is no mandatory local incorporation requirement solely for VAT registration.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Swiss law does not provide a 'check-the-box' regime. The AG is an independent legal subject taxed at entity level. Elective arrangements are limited to group tax consolidation at cantonal level ('Steuerkonsolidierung'), group value-added tax registration under Article 15 of the Federal VAT Act (close economic, financial and organisational links), and advance tax rulings issued by the competent cantonal tax administration and the FTA (including rulings on withholding tax, VAT and direct tax treatment of international service structures). No hybrid mismatch election is available.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: CHF 100,000 per year of taxable turnover from supplies made in Switzerland; foreign enterprises without a Swiss place of business are also liable if their Swiss-taxable supplies exceed CHF 100,000, or, in the case of certain cross-border services, if they exceed the worldwide CHF 100,000 threshold and the Swiss threshold is met. Voluntary registration is possible below the threshold.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Switzerland does not operate real-time VAT clearance or continuous transaction controls. No API-based fiscal stamping is required. Electronic invoices are permitted if they satisfy Swiss VAT invoice content requirements (Art. 26 of the Swiss VAT Act): supplier's identity and VAT UID, date, recipient, nature of supply, consideration and tax rate. For federal public procurement contracts, B2G e-invoicing is mandatory via the SIMAP portal in Peppol BIS 3.0 format. Invoices and electronic records must be retained for ten years.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating (tax-exempt with input VAT deduction) is available for: (i) goods physically transported out of Switzerland by the supplier, the recipient or a third party, evidenced by a Swiss Customs export declaration; (ii) services that are actually and economically used in a foreign country by a foreign business recipient or by a foreign private recipient, provided the recipient is established abroad and the service is not connected to Swiss domestic assets; (iii) services relating directly to exported goods (e.g. handling, transport, freight forwarding, and ancillary services) and typically also digital or animation/VFX services supplied to an overseas client where the benefit is obtained abroad. The supplier must as a rule obtain written confirmation from the foreign recipient, supporting transaction correspondence, and payment evidence to substantiate the foreign business purpose and the actual use abroad.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Swiss Customs Export Declaration (Aussgangszollanmeldung / déclaration en douane de sortie) filed via e-dec/Rhea
Bill of Lading / Air Waybill / CMR transport document or equivalent proof of shipment
Confirmation of foreign arrival or importation (foreign customs entry document, when obtained)
Bank transfer or SWIFT payment evidence from the foreign buyer / inward remittance evidence
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: False zero-rating claims are recharacterized as taxable domestic supplies; the FTA will retrospectively assess VAT at the applicable rate, disallow input VAT deductions, and impose default interest (4.0% per annum). Intentional or negligent tax evasion under Articles 70, 96 and 97 of the Swiss VAT Act attracts penalties up to double the tax amount evaded, plus administrative fines up to CHF 30,000; document falsification or fraudulent claiming of export exemptions can further trigger criminal prosecution and clawback of input VAT credits.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Swiss National Bank (SNB) acting together with the Swiss Financial Market Supervisory Authority (FINMA) for banking supervision and payment system oversight
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Switzerland maintains full current and capital account convertibility. The Swiss franc (CHF) is freely convertible; there are no exchange controls, no restrictions on inbound or outbound capital flows, and no statutory FX approval for ordinary cross-border transactions. Profit remittance and dividend distribution are unrestricted but trigger a 35% federal withholding tax, potentially reduced under an applicable double tax treaty. Practical frictions arise only from bank-level AML/KYC and sanctions screening, not from statutory FX regulation.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: No statutory surrender, repatriation, or mandatory conversion ratio applies to export receipts in Switzerland. Exporters may retain foreign currency indefinitely. Only statistical reporting obligations for identified cross-border payment thresholds and general tax/AML documentation requirements must be observed.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Rating: Low-Medium. Offshore digital EMIs (e.g., Wise B2B, Revolut Business, Airwallex) may be usable as supplementary cross-border collection and disbursement rails, but under Swiss law they cannot hold customer funds or provide main payment accounts to Swiss residents unless FINMA-authorized under the Banking Act or FinTech licence regime. A Swiss-licensed AG should not rely solely on an unregulated offshore EMI for primary treasury. Feasibility for low-value international vendor payments is Medium; for primary Swiss clearing and capital accounts it is Low.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Not statutorily mandatory for every director. Swiss banks may apply FINMA-recognized video identification and electronic signature onboarding for qualifying Swiss companies; however, tier-1 banks commonly require at least one authorized board signatory or the ultimate beneficial owner to attend an in-person interview or provide an apostilled notarial identification and original commercial register extract. Remote opening is possible but stricter for non-resident boards and for accounts handling large cross-border volumes. Practical compliance expectation: physical presence of the CEO or a delegated officer with notarized powers of attorney.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Ultimate beneficial owner located outside Switzerland or resident in a non-transparent jurisdiction
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Written beneficial ownership declaration, shareholder register extract, ultimate legal entity charts, foreign registry certificates, apostilled passports, proof of residence, notarized board resolution appointing signatories, and a source-of-wealth statement.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Suspected insufficient economic substance or artificial Swiss tax presence
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Lease agreement for Swiss premises, payroll and social insurance records (AHV/UVG), board minutes, detailed business plan, signed client service agreements, and audited financial statements evidencing Swiss operating substance.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Capital contributions sourced from cryptocurrency, Web3, or unregulated digital-asset proceeds
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Blockchain chain-analysis reports, on-chain and off-chain transaction audit trail, exchange statements showing fiat redemption, transaction hashes, tax filings or legal opinions covering Swiss characterization of digital assets, and formal source-of-funds explanation.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sanctions or politically exposed person (PEP) name flagged by automated screening
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Exact-name-match analysis, passport and date-of-birth verification, jurisdiction clarification, independent AML compliance opinion, negative sanctions/PEP search results from a regulated data vendor, and an affirmative statement that the relevant counterparty is not statutorily sanctioned or a PEP.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Disproportionately high projected payment volumes relative to stated share capital
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Cash flow forecast, signed production contracts, existing invoices, subcontractor agreements, and a narrative explanation of why an animation-VFX treasury requires elevated cross-border wire velocity.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound equity capital is routed by SWIFT MT103 / ISO 20022 using remittance text 'CAPITAL INCREASE – SHARE SUBSCRIPTION – [LEI/ENTITY REFERENCE]'. The foreign subscribing shareholder must instruct its bank to credit the Swiss AG's account with a final and irrevocable equity payment. The Swiss receiving bank will require: notarized capital-increase resolution, application for commercial register entry, auditor's confirmation of capital payment where applicable, source-of-funds evidence from the shareholder, and final beneficial ownership identification. For newly formed AGs, funds are held in a designated 'capital contribution account' and released only after commercial registration. Avoid blended purpose codes or loan/equity ambiguity; use a clean purpose code such as 'EQUITY CAPITAL ISSUE' to prevent routing delays.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Service-based disbursements for subcontracting, licenses, royalties, and animation production are cleared most efficiently through SWIFT MT103 with gpi tracking and, where applicable, SEPA credit transfer in EUR/CHF. For high-value or contractually material settlements, direct SWIFT wires with a full reference narrative are preferred; Wise B2B and comparable EMI rails can supplement low-value vendor payments provided each transaction carries a compliant purpose code and audit trail. For physical deliverables or film equipment supply, an irrevocable commercial letter of credit under UCP600 or a standby credit under ISP98 remains an acceptable but rarely necessary alternative for the 3D animation/commercial CGI model.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Outright FX forward contracts with FINMA-regulated Swiss banks or licensed counterparties
FX swaps combining spot and forward transactions on CHF/EUR/USD
Cross-currency interest rate swaps for medium-term international financing
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) only when a genuine commercial need and a regulated bank counterparty are present
Exchange-traded FX futures and options listed on SIX Swiss Exchange or recognized international venues

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Ordinary Annual General Meeting and approval of annual accounts (Jahresrechnung), profit appropriation and discharge of the Board of Directors
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Shareholders' General Meeting; no Commercial Register filing is required for a non-public AG
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within six months after the close of the financial year (Art. 699 para. 3 Swiss Code of Obligations)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Court-ordered General Meeting upon shareholder application; directors may be held liable for damages; persistent failure to convene can trigger formal default proceedings with the Commercial Register authority.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual corporate income and capital tax return covering federal, cantonal and communal profit taxes
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Cantonal Tax Authority of the registered office (federal profit tax is assessed within the cantonal procedure)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Generally within six to eight months after the business year end, as set by the applicable cantonal tax calendar; a 31 December year-end is commonly assessed by 30 June or 30 September of the following year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Default interest on any tax due; late-filing penalties up to approximately CHF 10,000 under cantonal law; tax may be assessed at the authority's discretion; continued refusal can expose management to criminal tax proceedings.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: VAT return and annual settlement for Swiss value added tax where annual taxable turnover exceeds CHF 100,000
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Swiss Federal Tax Administration (FTA / ESTV), Value Added Tax Division
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Periodic VAT returns are normally due within 60 days after the close of the VAT period; the annual settlement is submitted with the final return for the tax year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-payment interest and reminder surcharge of up to 5% of the VAT due; deliberate non-declaration can trigger tax penalty proceedings and director liability for withheld VAT.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Statutory audit report — ordinary or limited audit report, or unanimous opt-out resolution for a qualifying small AG
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Board and Shareholders; report retained in company records and available to tax authorities on request; no Commercial Register filing for private AGs
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Audit must be completed in time for the ordinary General Meeting; financial statements and audit report must be approved within the six-month statutory General Meeting window
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Without a valid audit report or opt-out resolution, the annual accounts cannot be lawfully approved; discharge resolutions are defective; directors and auditors may face civil liability.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Event-driven Commercial Register filings for changes to the Board of Directors, authorized signatories, share capital, registered office or articles of association
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Commercial Register Office of the canton of registered office (Handelsregisteramt)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 30 days after the corporate event; no fixed annual filing date applies because Swiss AGs are not subject to an annual confirmation statement
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Cantonal register penalties up to approximately CHF 5,000; forced registration may be ordered; persistent non-compliance with register duties can lead to administrative strike-off after formal warning proceedings.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: A Swiss AG must undergo an ordinary statutory audit if it is listed, regulated, or exceeds two of the following three thresholds in two consecutive financial years: balance sheet total above CHF 20 million, annual turnover above CHF 40 million, or more than 250 full-time employees on annual average. Other AGs require only a limited audit unless the company has fewer than 10 full-time employees on annual average and all shareholders unanimously opt out of audit for that financial year.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Statutory individual financial statements under the Swiss Code of Obligations (Art. 957 et seq.); Swiss GAAP FER or IFRS are permitted for presentation, and IFRS or Swiss GAAP FER is required for consolidation depending on group size and applicable exemption rules.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Swiss law does not impose a separate annual UBO confirmation return. The AG must maintain an internal beneficial-owner register and report any natural person with more than 25% of shares or voting rights to the federal Transparency Register within 30 days of a qualifying shareholding transfer or change. The company must update the register without delay and is entitled to request written confirmation from shareholders on an ad hoc basis.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Directors and Authorized Signatories
Minute Book containing Board and General Meeting minutes
In-house UBO Register and Transparency Register documentation where qualifying owners exist

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: CHF 600–3,500 per year (approx. USD 650–3,800), depending on canton and service level, including corporate domicile and administration support
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: CHF 3,000–9,000 for a limited audit of a small AG; CHF 12,000–40,000 for an ordinary audit of a mid-size animation/VFX company

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 8.5% federal profit tax rate on net profit after federal tax; equivalent to approximately 7.83% on pre-tax profit; combined federal plus cantonal/communal headline rates for a Swiss AG typically range from 12% to 21% depending on the canton of residence.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No general federal tax holiday; preferential effective rates result from cantonal IP-Box regimes for qualifying intangible income (relief of up to 50-90% depending on canton), additional cantonal R&D super-deductions up to 150%, and the federal/cantonal participation exemption for qualifying dividend and capital-gain income from substantial shareholdings.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Combined cantonal/federal corporate income tax return for legal entities ('Déclaration d'impôt pour personnes morales' / 'Steuererklärung für juristische Personen'), filed with the competent Cantonal Tax Administration through the canton's official e-filing portal; the federal portion is electronically forwarded to the Swiss Federal Tax Administration (ESTV/AFC/FTA) and is also accepted via the federal 'eTax' platform.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual; the tax period is the commercial fiscal year, with quarterly or fixed provisional tax instalments during the year based on the last final assessment.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Within six months after the close of the fiscal year under Art. 126 DBG/LIFD, unless the competent cantonal authority grants a filing extension; for a calendar-year AG, most cantons require delivery by 31 March or 15 April of the following tax year.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Legal entity identification: company name, seat, UID/IDE number, commercial register data, board of directors and group parent.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Enter the Swiss registered office and clearly indicate non-resident direct or beneficial owners in the ownership annex; attach the corporate group chart and disclose foreign control to ensure correct withholding-tax and treaty analysis.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Accounting period and applicable financial statements (Swiss GAAP, IFRS or minimum statutory presentation).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Use a twelve-month period aligned to the Swiss legal entity's standalone accounts; foreign-parent consolidations must not be substituted for the Swiss AG's individual taxable result.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross turnover from 3D/CGI animation production, visual-effects work, pre/post production services and related IP licensing.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report global contract revenue actually recognized by the Swiss AG; cross-border licence revenue paid by the foreign parent or affiliates must be valued at arm's length and listed separately for transfer-pricing reconciliation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net commercial profit before income tax per statutory profit-and-loss account.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Compute a standalone Swiss-entity result in Swiss francs; hedged foreign-currency animation contracts are recognized under Swiss GAAP or IFRS consistently, and the foreign parent cannot absorb losses or income of the Swiss AG.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Add-back of non-deductible expenses: federal direct tax, private member expenses, excessive board/related-party compensation, political contributions and value-shifting payments.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Add back foreign-parent service charges that lack a real Swiss business benefit or lack written support; payments characterized as hidden profit distributions to non-resident shareholders are taxable and become subject to Swiss federal withholding tax.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Utilized loss carryforwards and expiring loss-vintage years (maximum 7 years under Swiss federal tax law).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Only losses realized by the same Swiss legal entity are deductible; loss carryforwards of foreign predecessors, branches or shareholders cannot be transferred into the Swiss AG unless a Swiss statutory merger or reorganisation permits it.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable profit after adjustments, forming the common base for federal and cantonal/communal corporate income tax.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Document all participation-relief and IP-Box deductions claimed; the foreign shareholder's DTA status has no effect on the ordinary corporate tax liability but affects any subsequent distribution.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Capital stock and net equity schedule used for cantonal capital tax.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Show actual paid-in share capital, statutory reserves and retained earnings in CHF; shareholder loans or disguised equity may be recharacterized as equity if thin capitalization tests are failed.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late-filing procedural fines typically range from CHF 100 to CHF 10,000; default interest at statutory rates (approximately 3.5%-5% per annum) accrues on outstanding tax; after a formal reminder, the assessment office may estimate taxable profit and impose a cantonal late-filing surcharge, usually up to 5% of the assessed tax.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 35% Swiss federal anticipatory withholding tax (Verrechnungssteuer / impôt anticipé) on any direct, constructive or liquidating dividend paid by an AG, regardless of the shareholder's residence; participation relief reduces the company's corporate income tax base but does not eliminate the withholding obligation on distributions.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To apply a reduced DTA rate, the non-resident beneficial owner must obtain a valid Swiss-recognized tax residency certificate (Ansässigkeitsbescheinigung) from its own tax authority. The Swiss paying company may apply for exemption-at-source through the Swiss Federal Tax Administration's electronic e-Verrechnungssteuer portal; alternatively, the non-resident shareholder must file a refund claim with the ESTV within three years after the calendar year in which the withholding tax was accrued, attaching the DTA declaration, residency certificate and proof of beneficial ownership. Advance rulings are recommended for large or structured distributions.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Swiss domestic law imposes 35% withholding tax on interest on bonds, money-market paper and certain bank deposits paid by Swiss payers; ordinary commercial loan interest is generally not subject to Swiss statutory withholding tax. Outbound arm's-length royalty payments are not subject to Swiss statutory withholding tax, and under most Swiss DTAs royalties are taxable only in the resident state of the beneficial owner unless a Swiss permanent establishment exists.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: CHF 10 million aggregate annual cross-border related-party transactions is the general administrative threshold triggering the Swiss tax authority's request for Local File and Master File documentation; Country-by-Country Reporting becomes mandatory at CHF 900 million group consolidated revenue, with a CbCR notification filing.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Switzerland has no codified Economic Substance Regulation comparable to offshore centres; however, substantive corporate presence, local board decisions, qualified employees, operational premises and assumption of commercial risks are economic-substance criteria applied by the Swiss Federal Tax Administration and cantonal tax authorities to deny treaty benefits and prevent abusive shell structures, particularly for IP-holding and financing companies in Zug and Geneva.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Willfully omitting VFX production revenue, invoicing through fictitious foreign intermediaries, or submitting false balance sheets and intercompany statements to the Swiss tax authorities.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Reassessment of the evaded tax plus default interest; administrative fine of up to the amount of the evaded tax under Art. 175 DBG; in serious tax fraud under Art. 186 DBG, fine of up to three times the evaded tax and imprisonment of up to three years.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Board members who knowingly participated in the false declaration can be personally fined and imprisoned; they may also be held jointly civilly liable for the corporate tax shortfall and face attachment of personal assets or travel measures during criminal tax proceedings.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Abusive Transfer Pricing and Hidden Profit Distributions
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Selling 3D animation copyrights or characters to a foreign affiliate at below-market prices, paying duplicated management fees to a foreign parent, or operating with non-arm's-length intercompany loans and zero-interest facilities.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Mandatory arm's-length reallocation of profits and disallowance of excessive expense deductions; recharacterization as a hidden profit distribution triggers 35% federal withholding tax plus a 5% default interest charge; additional tax evasion penalties apply when intent is shown.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors approving false intercompany pricing or secret profit transfers are subject to director liability under Art. 754 CO for damage to the company and tax creditors; they may also face criminal liability for forgery and unlawful distribution of share capital, including imprisonment and travel bans in ongoing fraud investigations.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Withholding Tax Default on Profit Repatriation
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Distributing dividends or paying taxable bond-like interest to non-resident investors without deducting, reporting or remitting the 35% Swiss anticipatory tax.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The withholding tax remains owed by the Swiss company and is compulsorily collected by the ESTV together with default interest of approximately 5% per annum; procedural fines and, in cases of constructive distribution, gross-up of the distribution are also imposed.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors can become personally liable for the unremitted withholding tax when they knowingly ordered the payment; criminal prosecution may result in imprisonment of up to five years under aggravated tax fraud and, in cross-border cases, an automatic passport or travel-ban measure pending final judgment.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company, Treaty Abuse and AML Substance Failure
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using a Zug or Geneva AG as an opaque holding vehicle for foreign strategic decisions, with no Swiss staff, no Swiss management meetings, no business premises and no transparent beneficial-ownership filing; channelling royalties or dividends solely to obtain DTA protection or banking confidentiality.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Denial of treaty reductions and refunds; retroactive assessment of 35% withholding tax on hidden distributions; tax-reassessment penalties; under the Swiss Anti-Money Laundering Act and FinIA, shell-type structures without adequate UBO screening can attract fines of up to CHF 500,000 and mandatory reporting to the MROS.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Foreign shadow directors and ultimate beneficial owners can be treated as de facto directors and subjected to Swiss criminal sanctions for money laundering, forgery and unlawful asset management; civil liability reaches personal wealth when the corporate veil is pierced for abuse and personal guarantees, with travel bans and executives' residence restrictions imposed during active proceedings.
